system.name: World-In-World
system.one_liner: An open platform that benchmarks generative world models by closed-loop embodied task success rather than visual quality.

content.variant_note: a question banner, a three-zone platform band (models, platform with a policy, four task cards) and an answer banner holding a leaderboard tile and three schematic plots
content.argues: World models should be ranked by embodied task success, not visual quality; the figure poses the question and shows the platform, leaderboard and scaling findings.
content.subject: A closed-loop platform linking video world models to an embodied policy and four task environments, with a leaderboard and three schematic result plots.

lessons.what_to_learn: Frame a benchmark teaser with a question banner on top and an answer banner below; in between put the platform box with a policy icon whose arrows join model logos on one side to task cards on the other, then close with a leaderboard tile and tick-less schematic plots that reuse the logos as markers.
lessons.suits: Benchmark or platform papers that want one overview showing the question, the platform, the tasks, the models and the headline findings.

evidence: We introduce the first open benchmark to evaluate world models by closed-loop task success
analyze the link between task success and visual quality, and investigate scaling laws
World-in-World provides a unified online planning strategy and a standardized action API

summary: World-In-World is an open platform that benchmarks generative world models by how much they help an embodied agent succeed in closed-loop tasks, instead of by visual quality. Figure 1 is a teaser in three bands. A gradient banner asks 'Do Better Video Models Lead to Higher Embodied Success?'. Below, a light-blue zone lists six video models by logo and name, a brown-outlined platform box holds a purple robot policy with arrows labelled Embodied Policy, Unified Action and Closed-Loop Interaction, and a light-purple zone shows four task cards (Active Recognition, Navigation, Question Answering, Manipulation) with scene renders. A dark banner states 'World models are ranked by embodied success, not flawless visuals' over a leaderboard screenshot and three schematic plots for data scaling, inference-time scaling and correlation.
summary_zh: World-In-World 是一个开放平台，用闭环具身任务成功率而非画面质量来评测生成式世界模型。图为三段式预告：顶部提问横幅，中间左为视频模型徽标、居中为带机器人策略的平台框、右为四张任务卡，底部深色横幅给出排行榜与三张示意曲线。
notes: No body paragraph mentions the figure; roles come from the caption, abstract and figure text. Prior kinds kept (contribution-mosaic first). Arrow meanings are read from the labels and layout: models to policy, policy to models (Unified Action), policy to tasks (Embodied Policy), tasks to policy (Closed-Loop Interaction). The two gradient banners are placed bitmaps in the digest. The light-grey fill #ededed in the digest could not be matched to a single element.
